spatialBenefitAssessment: Current candidate does not yet pass the gate. Looking behind lockers reveals a continuous shelf, but the mechanism chiefly hides a simple authorization diagram behind doors and replays the video’s fixed fail/repair/rerun sequence. Stale results are a temporal relationship. A salvage attempt needs a user-controlled access-path counterfactual that tests harness coverage, not just a more attractive back view.

findings.issue: Orbit plus a fixed ownership-check installation does not add a convincing investigation of harness behavior.
findings.requestedChange: Replace the one-way repair with an inspectable two-route fixture: a tested front access path and an alternate rear access path to the same invoice. Let the first control change enforcement placement (front path versus shared resource boundary) and the second run both route probes. Keep both routes visible in an open cutaway, and let the user inspect why a local gate leaves a bypass. Explain the narrow coverage of those checks. If this cannot be made legible without added cards or clutter, omit the 3D candidate.
findings.evidence: startRun always runs the same two probes; startInstall installs one partition permanently until Reset. Recommended Astra transcript already shows both tenant expectations, stale results and rerun. Front/back concealment alone supplies little new harness understanding.

findings.issue: The geometry does not substantiate both asserted request results.
findings.requestedChange: Make each tested request visibly reach the same target invoice or return an inspectable response token; preserve owner access when installing the authorization boundary. Keep an open view of the stopping point and returned artifact. Explicitly identify the boundary as a metaphor for an ownership predicate, not a requirement for physically separate tenant storage.
findings.evidence: poseRun moves Invoice_A only with probe B; probe A merely advances and retracts, yet endRun always sets A to pass. intent acknowledges A does not retrieve its invoice. A shared shelf is not itself evidence of missing software authorization.

findings.issue: Only the closed initial state has browser evidence; essential rear geometry and result-lamp picks are unverified.

Review method: source/transcript reading and supplied image inspection only; no shared browser use, independent runtime test, video playback or implementation changes. Coordinator owns final verification.
